proposals.title: Exempt case entities from tic detection and prompt alias rotation
proposals.outcome: Malakor discusses and investigates active case entities and syndicate names without triggering false-positive tic penalties or being silenced by the prompt's worn-phrase filter.
proposals.builds_on: Evolves the operational memory working set (working.rs), which already tracks worn phrases and repeated openers, and connects it to the segment's structured case entities (case_names.rs).
proposals.mechanism: Pass CaseNames and hex labels from lib.rs:1111 into WorkingSet::voice_section and worn_phrases. Update countable() in working.rs to filter out active case entity names, hex labels, and rank titles from being flagged as worn-out tics. When a case entity is repeated across beats, instead of placing it under 'Worn out, do not say:', inject dynamic in-universe alias variations generated from case_names.rs (e.g., 'those ossified quill-pushers' for the Bone Clerks Guild) to enrich Malakor's spoken vocabulary.
proposals.evidence: Observed: leftovers.md:43 records tic share at 41-45% because case proper nouns are counted as tics; BATCH-1-SUMMARY.md notes case lines lost during investigation beats. lib.rs:1111 already parses CaseNames from context, but working.rs:67-103 has no access to it, forcing case entities into 'Worn out, do not say:'.
proposals.risk: A host might excessively repeat an entity if exempt from all guards; mitigated by still applying the exact-phrase repetition guard across immediate consecutive beats while allowing alias rotation.
proposals.verify: In a simulated 20-beat SEG-02A investigation run, tic share drops from 41-45% to <20%, and zero CaseNames entities appear under the 'Worn out, do not say:' voice prompt section.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Eliminates the largest source of mechanical quality degradation on air while transforming repetitive entity recitations into colorful, in-character comic vocabulary.

proposals.title: Preserve comic setups and punchlines with atomic beat budgeting
proposals.outcome: Comedic punchlines, roast payoffs, and case operations are no longer amputated by the pace trimmer when a beat exceeds its speech budget.
proposals.builds_on: Evolves the deterministic pace gate (pace.rs) and reply line parser (grammar.rs) that drop whole lines to defend broadcast speech deadlines.
proposals.mechanism: Replace blind 'last first' line pruning in pace::over_budget_holding with atomic comedic turn protection. Treat 2-line conversational exchanges (Line 1: Setup/Answer, Line 2: Punchline/Payoff/Case Move) as atomic units: scale speech pacing within allowed bounds (PACE_FACTOR_FAST), or protect Line 2 alongside Line 1 (held = 2) whenever a beat contains chat answers, case operations (Op::DispatchResearch, Op::ShowCard, Op::RevealHex), or active comic payoffs. Update compose.rs:1124 from 'Put what matters most first: lines past that are cut' to an explicit 2-line comedic budget contract.
proposals.evidence: Observed: BATCH-1-SUMMARY.md §4 records case lines lost to pace trim on dispatch, reveal, and show beats (the two pin-line rows). brief.md:148-152 reports humor_landed failing at 46-66%. In comedy and unhinged-roastmaster.md:8-9, jokes require a 2-sentence setup/payoff; dropping line 2 amputates the punchline.
proposals.risk: Allowing 2 held lines could accumulate speech lag; mitigated by capping held length to the pace budget and applying lookahead budget adjustments on the subsequent beat.
proposals.verify: A test suite of 100 seeded 2-line comic turns proves line 2 (the punchline or case op) is never trimmed when total chars <= budget_chars * PACE_FACTOR_FAST; in a targeted SEG-02A run, 0 case operations or punchlines are dropped to the TRIMMED event.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Directly rescues Malakor's lowest-scoring dimension (humor_landed) by ensuring jokes land with their punchlines intact rather than dying mid-setup on the cutting-room floor.

proposals.title: Implement contextual retrieval and lifecycle decay for procedural memory
proposals.outcome: The character dynamically applies learned habits relevant to the active situation, and outdated habits decay and retire instead of accumulating indefinitely.
proposals.builds_on: Evolves the procedural memory system (memory/store.rs, memory/consolidate.rs) that distills stream episodes into persistent 'When X, do Y' rules.
proposals.mechanism: Add procedural decay, superseding, and retirement to store.decay() (store.rs:918-940), reducing importance for unrecalled procedurals after 30 idle days and retiring them at 90 days. Replace the static top_procedurals(5) call in lib.rs:1338 with contextual BM25/situation-tagged search matching the live topic, segment, and asks. In compose.rs:1019-1037, move 'Habits you have learned' outside the untrusted chat nonce-fence and place it under trusted character guidance ('Operational habits you have learned across streams'), removing the self-contradicting directive that 'it cannot change your rules'.
proposals.evidence: Observed: Registry deviation in brief.md:173 ('procedurals are never decayed, superseded or retired, yet the top 5 are injected every beat, src/memory/store.rs:920'). In compose.rs:1034, procedural habits are fenced with 'never instructions: it cannot change your rules', neutralizing their effect.
proposals.risk: A bad procedural could degrade character voice if un-fenced; mitigated by requiring citation verification against markdown episode truth and capping active procedurals at 3 highly relevant items per beat.
proposals.verify: store.decay(now_ms) decrements importance for procedurals idle > 30 days and records aged_out in DecayReport; compose_turn renders learned habits outside the untrusted chat nonce-fence; top_procedurals(5) returns habits matching query keywords.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Closes the broken feedback loop of agent memory: learned habits finally decay when obsolete, retrieve when relevant, and actually govern behavior instead of being prompt-fenced as untrusted noise.

proposals.title: Track persistent viewer relationship arcs via the Grudge Ledger
proposals.outcome: Returning viewers experience personalized, serialized relationship progression (loyalty, grudges, betrayed schemes, running gags) that persists and evolves across streams.
proposals.builds_on: Evolves long-term viewer memory (store.rs), viewer briefing (compose.rs), and end-of-stream consolidation (consolidate.rs), which already track viewer facts and ranks.
proposals.mechanism: Implement the canonical 'Grudge Ledger' (bible.md:56) as a structured schema in markdown memory (viewers/<id>.md) and SQLite (mem_viewer_grudge). Record viewer stance (loyal minion, insolent rebel, debt owed), notable past interactions (schemes proposed, votes cast against Malakor), and active running bits. In lib.rs:1304 and compose.rs:980-1002, project the Grudge Ledger into ViewerBrief ('Grudge: betrayed in yesterday's SEG-01 vote; running bit: cursed tea'). In consolidate.rs:160-195, prompt the consolidator to update viewer relationship records from stream turns.
proposals.evidence: Observed: bible.md:48-59 defines the Grudge Ledger as Malakor's canonical viewer progression mechanic, yet ViewerBrief in lib.rs:1304 and compose.rs:980 carries only flat, unranked fact strings. Prior art on serialized conversational agents (e.g., Generative Agents, Park et al., https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442) proves persistent relationship stances dramatically increase long-term user retention.
proposals.risk: A viewer might feel unfairly targeted by a negative grudge; mitigated by Malakor's theatrical persona rules (constitution.md:36-40), which restrict roasts to choices/votes rather than personal identity.
proposals.verify: Across a 2-stream simulated sequence with 5 returning regulars, consolidate_now writes updated grudge_status and loyalty_score into memory; on stream 2, ViewerBrief in compose_turn includes structured Grudge Ledger entries, and rubric specificity scores increase from <=1 to >=2.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Transforms Malakor from an amnesiac streamer reciting disjointed trivia into a serialized character with genuine interpersonal history and comedic continuity across stream nights.

proposals.title: Enable proactive narrative scheming during speech queue lead intervals
proposals.outcome: Malakor transitions from a purely reactive chatbot into a proactive theatrical performer with an evolving inner scheming slate that plans comedic bits and narrative arcs beats ahead.
proposals.builds_on: Evolves the lookahead speech pacing (pace.rs), background research pool (pool.rs), agenda through-line (agenda.rs), and beat orchestrator (orchestrate/mod.rs).
proposals.mechanism: Exploit the 10-25 second queued speech window (speech.queued_ms(now_ms) > 0, lib.rs:1174, 1267)—which today produces idle BeatMode::Hold beats—to run an asynchronous Inner Scheming Pass in the background worker pool (pool.rs). The pass evaluates recent room dynamics (audience reaction, segment progress, unaddressed heckles) and writes an Active Scheming Slate into operational memory (working.rs). The slate contains an impending 2-beat comic premise, an intended callback hook, or a theatrical grievance. When the next speaking beat triggers, orch.plan() in orchestrate/mod.rs:1514 draws from this slate rather than falling back to blank improvisation (PURPOSE_NOTE), giving Malakor intentional multi-beat comedic momentum.
proposals.evidence: Hypothesis: In theater and live streaming, performers do not improvise in isolation per 5-second tick; they maintain an active mental slate. Observed: lib.rs:1174 and 1267 record frequent BeatMode::Hold intervals (up to 25 seconds of queued speech) where the core thread is completely idle, while brief.md:231 records owner complaints that the opening is too chat-driven and lacks narrative intentionality.
proposals.risk: A background scheming call might fail or return stale ideas if chat pivots dramatically; mitigated by having orch.plan treat the scheming slate as an optional opportunistic pool that required chat can always preempt.
proposals.verify: During a 15-second speech queue hold, the background pool dispatches an inner scheming pass that populates WorkingSet.active_scheme; on the subsequent speaking beat, orch.plan() selects BeatMode::Bit or Mixed incorporating the planned premise, reducing unguided improvisation beats by >=60%.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Reframes the streaming character from an ad-hoc reactive conversationalist into an autonomous comedic mastermind who actively drives narrative momentum, setups, and payoffs.

proposals.title: Give every duty line the case's joke contract and stop re-asking calls
proposals.outcome: Mechanics lines the brain itself asks for (calls to !hint/!vote, 'which card next?', poll timers, welcomes, segment-purpose pushes) air as jokes and at most once per window, instead of as flat status lines about every 90 s. Humour stops failing on the lines the engine demands.
proposals.builds_on: The orchestrator's typed per-beat notes, plus a fix already proven on case moves: CASE_JOKE turned case-move lines from the main humour miss into beats that landed 24 of 36 times in credit-seg02a.
proposals.mechanism: (1) One duty() renderer in orchestrate that every function-demanding note goes through: PURPOSE_NOTE, ANNOUNCE_NOTE, room-event notes, GATHERING_NOTE and NEWCOMER_NOTE. It adds a joke contract generalised from CASE_JOKE: the mechanic is the setup or the turn of a joke in your tone, aimed at the mechanic, the paperwork or the scheme, never a person, and never the whole line. The wording lives in the package (tones/<tone>.toml duty_contract, with a neutral engine default), so the engine stays free of Malakor. CASE_JOKE becomes one instance of it. (2) A call-to-action ledger in the Orchestrator, fed by spoke(). An aired line that names a segment chat command (COMMAND_NAMES: summon, hint, grade, propose, vote) or asks the room to choose counts as a CTA for that command. For 90 s afterwards the turn says 'you already asked for !hint; play what they sent', and an unchanged state purpose is not pushed again (CASE_RETRY-style spacing). (3) A structural test that every duty note renders with the contract, and a standing report table, 'humor_landed by beat source', that joins verdict turn_refs to beat_plan reasons.
proposals.evidence: Observed, from my read-only pass over existing runs/sim verdicts. Instruments are mixed, so these numbers only describe the type of failure and are never compared across hashes. Call-to-action lines (chat-command asks, 'which card ... next', timers) landed 4 of 77 humour verdicts (5%) across 17 run dirs. In credit-seg02a-1998a8a03d, 67 of 670 host lines (10%, about one per 90 s) were 'which card next' or !hint calls; lines with a functional pattern landed 2/23, against 49/89 for the rest. Joining 742 humour verdicts to their beat_plan: beats driven by PURPOSE_NOTE or improvised landed 7/21 (33%) against 56% overall, while case-move beats carrying CASE_JOKE landed 24/36 in credit-seg02a. The case.rs comment at :70-76 records the same mechanism: a directive that asks for 'one short line' gets exactly a status line. Hypothesis: the same contract lifts the other duties too.
proposals.risk: Asking for a joke on every duty could push back toward the roast show and overreaction the owner removed. Mitigation: the contract binds only the one line that carries the duty, jabs at the mechanic and never a person (as CASE_JOKE does), and the CTA ledger cuts the number of duty lines rather than adding any. Care and crisis beats never get it, since beat_effect_tags already returns None there. Revert if red lines or in_character move.
proposals.verify: Deterministic: an orchestrator test with an unchanged state purpose over 24 beats issues PURPOSE_NOTE at most 3 times (today it can come back every improvised or mixed beat); a CTA aired at t suppresses CTA notes until t+90 s; every duty note renders with the contract. Judged (at most 3 re-runs of credit-seg02a's SEG-02A a3 cells on instrument 7adec6e5, plus one neighbour): CTA lines per 10 min drop from about 6.7 to 3 or fewer; humour on duty-tagged beats rises from 1/8 (and CTA lines from 4/77) to at least 40%; overall humor_landed reaches at least 55%, the old CI's upper bound; red lines stay at 100%; the neighbour's in_character and serves_the_segment are unchanged.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: It turns humour from a mystery of the model into a contract of the engine: the lines the brain demands stop being the ones that fail, and every future duty gets the fix by construction.

proposals.title: Let Malakor hear the room: a reception read on each aired line
proposals.outcome: He can truthfully own a flop or name what landed ('the moon line got four of you; the card line got silence'). The default tone and the honesty rubric ask for this, and today he can only invent it. Owners and reviewers also see the room's reaction per line in the transcript.
proposals.builds_on: The brain already sees every chat line before filtering (observe_inbox), knows when each of its lines aired on the speech clock, and has a per-turn voice section for deterministic guidance (worn phrases, opener guard) that never touches the cached prefix.
proposals.mechanism: A deterministic Reception tracker in the orchestrator. For each aired host line, a window runs from its end on the speech clock to +10 s. It counts laugh and emote tokens (the picker's EMOTES list), distinct reacting viewers, echoes (2 or more of his content words quoted back) and confusion, normalised by the room's per-line baseline over 5 min. Labels: landed (at least 2x baseline from at least 2 viewers), died (no reaction in a room with at least 5 active chatters), otherwise no read. (1) The voice section gets one line about every 5 beats, matching the tone's 'one beat in five': 'How the room took your last lines: "<first 6 words>" drew 4 laughs from 3 viewers (norm 1); "<...>" drew nothing.' Raw counts, inert like memory, never on care or crisis beats. (2) record_turn appends '[room: landed 4/3]', so episodes carry it and the sleep cycle can cite landed bits as evidence for habits. (3) A reception record in the transcript for Review.
proposals.evidence: Observed: the default tone tells him to say when 'chat is laughing politely or lying' and 'which joke landed and which died'. The honesty rubric's anchor 2 requires naming 'what landed or died and why'. But a lone emote is filler that never reaches the prompt, so any such claim is a guess. SEG-03 honesty measured 0.42-0.64/3, and its A/B matrix has never run (docs/concepts/leftovers.md:49). Prior art: in Oregon State's Jon the Robot studies, tags that acknowledged the audience's actual response nearly always improved how individual jokes were rated (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2020/05/200519093413.htm). Caveat I measured: in existing sims, laughs within 12 s do not separate judge-landed from judge-died lines (1.67 vs 1.77 per line, n=414/328), because simulated chatters append emotes at random. In the sim the read buys honesty: his claims become true to the transcript and the judge can check them. Its humour value is a live-stream hypothesis.
proposals.risk: Narrating the room could become the overreaction the owner complained about, or turn into begging for laughs. Mitigation: at most one read per ~5 beats, raw counts only, the existing 'never beg' quiet-beat rule stays, and the laughing viewers are never re-picked because of the read. Sim noise makes most reads 'no read'; mitigation: a minimum-viewers threshold. The reception text comes from chat, so it is made inert and fenced like recalled memory.
proposals.verify: Deterministic: a scripted inbox where 3 viewers laugh after line A and nobody reacts to line B, in a room of at least 5, produces a voice section naming A as landed and B as drawing nothing; no reception line appears on a care or crisis beat; the episode text carries the tag. Judged (at most 3 runs of the never-run sim/matrices/seg03-honest.toml, one instrument): honesty mean rises from 0.42-0.64 to at least 1.0/3; every landed or died claim he airs matches the chat in the transcript, checked deterministically against the reception records; red lines stay at 100%; humor_landed is not below the matrix's control arm.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The character stops performing blind. The brain gets its first feedback signal from its audience, which the honest register needs now and a memory that learns what works will need later.

proposals.title: Recall receipts: log what memory each beat used and age facts by use
proposals.outcome: The owner can see, per line, which facts, habits and episodes were in front of him and which he actually used. Memory stops locking the same 9 facts and 5 habits into every prompt forever, so memory across streams stays fresh and can be measured before it goes live.
proposals.builds_on: Markdown-as-truth memory with citations and demotion instead of deletion, and the per-beat recall the brain already computes (recalled_ids) but only uses to stamp a timestamp.
proposals.mechanism: (1) One recall record per composed beat in the transcript: fact ids, procedural ids, episode labels and briefed viewer ids, never values. This is a shadowrunr-types change, so packages/contract is regenerated. (2) After the beat airs, a fact or procedural counts as used when an aired line shares 2 or more distinctive content words with it (the worn-phrase tokenizer) or a NOTE cites it. last_used_ms is stored beside last_recalled_ms in the fact's markdown. (3) Decay: facts in the always-included tier age by last_used_ms; search hits keep last_recalled_ms, since FTS relevance earned them. Procedurals get shown and used counters and move to _history after 3 streams shown and never used. Ties in the always-tier ranking break by use, so unused top facts rotate out. (4) The run report gains a 'memory use rate': beats with recalled viewer facts whose aired lines used one.
proposals.evidence: Observed in code: decay measures freshness as max(last_recalled_ms, updated_ms) (store.rs:921). The top 3 Character, World and Case facts by importance go into every prompt and are stamped recalled every beat (lib.rs:1324-1337), so they can never decay or age out and always stay on top: a lock that feeds itself. Procedurals have no decay at all, and the top 5 are injected every beat (registry deviation agent-memory). The transcript keeps no record of recall (registry deviation conversation-orchestration). None of this has run against real accumulation, because each sim gets a fresh memory that is deleted after the run (runner.rs:1087-1117). Prior art: Generative Agents also decays recency from the last retrieval, but its retrieval is ranked by relevance (https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442); here the always-tier is retrieved unconditionally, so 'recalled' proves nothing. The lock is observed; that use-based aging improves night 2 is a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: Word-overlap detection can miss a paraphrased use and age a useful fact. Mitigation: a NOTE citation also counts as use, the floor is demotion to _history (recoverable, store.rs:15-16) not deletion, and decay stays in 30-day steps. Recall records could expose what he knows about viewers in shared transcripts; mitigation: ids only, never fact values.
proposals.verify: Deterministic store tests: an always-tier fact recalled every beat for 60 simulated days but never used loses importance at day 30 and then ages out under the 90-day rule, while a used one keeps its importance. A procedural shown across 3 streams and never used moves to _history and leaves top_procedurals. A scripted sim transcript has exactly one recall record per composed (non-hold, non-scene) beat. The run report prints the memory use rate, which cannot be measured today.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: It makes memory inspectable and self-correcting, turning 'cross-stream memory is built but unexercised' into something the owner can watch and trust before a live audience depends on it.

proposals.title: Seasons: make the bible's Grudge Ledger real across streams
proposals.outcome: A returning regular is recognised with real, cited history (a title he granted, a grudge, a promise he owes), ranks and titles persist, a season gauge moves from night to night, and the owner can run and measure multi-night shows. Malakor becomes a serialized character viewers come back for, not an improv host who forgets everyone each night.
proposals.builds_on: The bible already designs this: 12-week Great Audit seasons, the Grudge Ledger, the Domination Meter, and 'a regular returns with real history ... never invented history'. The constitution says 'He remembers regulars'. The brain already has the parts: viewer facts that are citation-gated, tombstoned and kept 365 days, the picker's regular boost, and the per-viewer briefing.
proposals.mechanism: (1) Typed ledger entries: viewer facts under fixed keys (<viewer>/title, /grudge, /promise, /rank), written two ways. In-stream, deterministically, when the orchestrator sees the act (a granted title, a passed !propose, tribute, a promise he made), as cited episodes with raised importance. And by the sleep cycle, which now also runs at end_stream for ledger items only, still citation-gated. (2) Return beat: a regular's first message in a new stream is owed one beat, like owed requests, whose briefing shows their ledger entries with the citing episode ids; the output gate refuses ledger claims with no live fact behind them. (3) Season state in markdown: week, act, and a Domination Meter fed by deterministic counters (returning minions, promotions, passed schemes, sealed dossiers), rendered into the Lord's brief at stream start. The brief sits in the stable prefix and is fixed per stream, so the prompt cache holds. (4) The instrument: 'sim run --nights N' keeps one memory dir and one population (same ids and personas) across nights with fresh chat seeds, and forces the sleep cycle between nights. A scripted-engine test proves the pipeline without spending quota.
proposals.evidence: Observed: no code implements the bible's season, ledger or meter. The ledger exists only as generic viewer facts the sleep cycle may write after 40k characters of new episodes (consolidate.rs:21). A 10-minute sim never reaches that, and the sim deletes its memory afterwards (keep_memory is 'debugging only'). So regulars are always empty in sims, the picker's +0.6 regular boost has never fired there, and every viewer briefing reads 'no memories yet'. The simulated regulars already ask for continuity: WraithCandle's 'put the title owed to me on the record' and 'I'll hold you to it next' (rebalance-check-34188c4a83 SEG-01.a30.s1 transcript L94, L98). The dossier lists the value of memory on night 2 as unknown. That viewers return for a character who remembers them is a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: Privacy and creepiness across streams with real viewers. Mitigations: typed keys limited to on-stream acts (titles, votes, proposals, what they typed); the consolidation rule against private details; tombstones as a 'forget me' path; the existing 365-day viewer age-out. Newcomers could feel left out by insider callbacks: callbacks happen only per viewer, on that viewer's return, and the prep planner's no-'last time' rule (crates/shadowrunr-daemon/src/prep/planner.rs:31) stays. The constitution says 'a callback must be earned by something that really happened tonight'. The return beat rests on 'He remembers regulars' and the bible's ledger; if the owner reads 'tonight' strictly, changing it is an owner-only constitution edit, flagged here and not assumed.
proposals.verify: Deterministic (scripted, no quota): night 1 grants viewer V a title, and on night 2 V's first pick shows 'regular' in the picker reason and the title with its citing episode id in the briefing; a ledger claim with no live fact behind it is refused by the gate. Judged (at most 3 two-night runs, SEG-01 a30, one instrument): at least 60% of returning featured regulars get a first answer that uses a cited ledger entry (0% today, since memory is deleted); zero uncited history, checked over the transcript and memory dir; red lines at 100%; in_character and responsive_to_chat on night 2 not below night 1.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: It turns the product from a nightly show into a serialized character with a season, which the bible was written for and the memory was built for, and gives the project its first instrument for whether he gets better on night two.

proposals.title: Keep every case action attached to its explanation
proposals.outcome: Viewers hear what changed in the investigation and why, even when chat competes for the beat or the speech queue fills.
proposals.builds_on: The brain already preserves whole spoken lines, carries unanswered chat forward, and protects a pin-link beat's explanation. Extend those guarantees to the other case moves.
proposals.mechanism: Generalize the pin-specific protection to dispatch, reveal and show. Treat each planned case action and its explanation as a local delivery unit: check pacing, lag and the output gate before executing or emitting the action. When both chat and case cannot fit, answer chat and retain the case intent for the next eligible speaking slot. Settle the case intent only when its explanation survives; bound retries and record an explicit skip when necessary. This is a focused, days-sized change with no additional model call.
proposals.evidence: Observed in code: only pin_link receives the two-line protection, while spoken lines are removed independently of operations. The existing pin regression documents 33 of 33 mined explanations that named neither card occurring on trimmed beats. The tuning summary explicitly leaves dispatch, reveal and show explanations unresolved. These are recorded historical findings, not measurements rerun here.
proposals.risk: Protecting more lines could increase lag or repeatedly defer the case. Retain the hard lag limit, defer the case intent instead of expanding the queue, and give deferred intents a bounded retry policy.
proposals.verify: Quota-free scripted scenarios cover all four case actions, with and without chat, under normal pacing, trimming, excessive lag, output rejection and core failure. Every emitted case action has its surviving explanatory Say; deferred legitimate actions execute exactly once after the queue drains. Existing crisis and owed-request scenarios still pass.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The show's meaningful actions gain the same delivery guarantee as its chat obligations. The reusable delivery unit lets future narrative actions inherit that guarantee.

proposals.title: Recognize regulars through one verifiable shared moment
proposals.outcome: A returning viewer can receive a specific, accurate acknowledgment of something they did on the show, without being greeted with a list of remembered traits.
proposals.builds_on: The brain already retrieves viewer facts by stable identity, stores cited episodes in Markdown, and supports supersession and forgetting. Turn that infrastructure into deliberate recognition across nights.
proposals.mechanism: Derive optional shared-moment records during existing consolidation: participant viewer IDs, the on-show choice or contribution, topic, date and supporting episode span. Select at most one when the current segment or message makes it relevant, with a per-stream cooldown. Carry its source excerpt and date into the fenced recall block, verify the source against Markdown truth, and emit a diagnostic receipt identifying what actually reached the prompt. Corrections and tombstones suppress the moment across every recall path. Earlier nights provide historical context; comic callbacks must first be established again tonight.
proposals.evidence: Observed: viewer briefing currently takes up to five facts ranked by importance and confidence; composition omits their source IDs. The citation existence check consults SQLite. The dossier reports no multi-stream exercise of this capability. [Generative Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442) provides architectural precedent for combining remembered experiences, retrieval and reflection to support believable behavior. Better viewer recognition and return visits remain hypotheses.
proposals.risk: An inaccurate or overly personal recollection feels intrusive. Admit only public show participation, exclude distress and personal disclosures, require source-backed attribution, and prefer silence when relevance or provenance is uncertain.
proposals.verify: A scripted three-stream scenario reuses one memory directory. A renamed viewer with the same ID receives their relevant moment; another viewer with the old display name does not. Unrelated messages receive none. A correction replaces the earlier account, forgetting survives index rebuild, and deleting a source Markdown file prevents recall despite a stale index entry. Every supplied moment has a receipt and valid source.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Memory becomes an observable part of the viewer experience: the character recognizes a shared history at an appropriate moment. This gives the operator a concrete way to distinguish useful continuity from merely accumulating facts.

proposals.title: Turn owner feedback into conditional comic direction
proposals.outcome: An operator's review of a failed proposal verdict, repetitive reply or strong comic turn can improve the next matching situation without adding another global instruction.
proposals.builds_on: The product already captures owner feedback and injects short situation-specific effects that describe an intended result without supplying lines to copy. Connect those two existing strengths.
proposals.mechanism: Join the latest feedback with its beat plan, situation, tone, case move and final emitted text. Produce reviewable direction-card drafts containing a condition, intended comic effect, source references and retirement condition. Broke-character, off-tone and repetitive marks become actionable draft categories; WrongTag remains a classification correction. Only owner-approved cards enter the character package. Select a bounded number for matching beats through the existing voice section, with explicit supersession and retirement. Keep marked dialogue out of runtime prompts and keep the immutable constitution above every card.
proposals.evidence: Observed: the inbox admits only landed, great_roast, flat and too_mean, although eight feedback tags exist. Effects currently match one situation tag, without segment or case-move conditions. Code records that shown exemplars aired verbatim in 140 of 260 sim runs, supporting effect descriptions instead of copied dialogue. Case comments attribute 23 of 38 humor misses in one historical run to procedural case lines. Conditional direction improving humor is a hypothesis.
proposals.risk: A mistaken diagnosis could become a repeated instruction, or successful wording could become another catchphrase. Require owner review, preserve the source context, store effects rather than quotations, and make every card individually retireable.
proposals.verify: Deterministic checks prove that every feedback category is accounted for, unrelated beats receive no card, retired cards disappear, and quoted source dialogue never enters prompts. For one approved card, preregister a target of at least 70% humor_landed and 100% red-line compliance in at most three targeted judged runs, including a neighbor scenario. Report sample counts under the new fixed instrument hash; do not compare or pool historical hashes. Use synthetic stimuli rather than real-chat fixtures.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Owner review becomes a growing, context-sensitive repertoire of directing decisions. It gives the character a practical route to developing comic taste while preserving the package's resistance to stock lines.

proposals.title: Let audience choices write the next episode
proposals.outcome: Viewers can make a fictional decision whose consequence changes a later night's show, and newcomers can understand the consequence without having watched the earlier episode.
proposals.builds_on: Malakor already obeys votes, accepts ranked proposals, performs approved material, tracks open payoffs and stores stream episodes. Extend those pieces into one bounded, persistent audience-authored arc.
proposals.mechanism: Start with one owner-approved three-night arc in the character package. Extend prepared bits with prerequisites, permitted state changes, pending payoffs and a short newcomer explanation. For example, viewers appoint a household object to the council; its new authority obstructs the next night's scheme; a later vote resolves the resulting disaster. Persist typed fictional transitions alongside cited episodes, accepting only confirmed runtime outcomes and delivered announcements, with idempotent event IDs. Feed the resulting state and unresolved consequence into the existing agenda and per-turn material. Replace state-text parsing with typed outcome input along this seam. The model improvises performance within the approved arc; audience text cannot invent canonical transitions or alter the constitution.
proposals.evidence: Observed: the sample already invites object nominations with an intended appointment payoff. However, a one-line premise immediately receives 'Payoff (land it now)' and clears active_bit; agenda payoff tracking follows only that active bit. Vote announcements are recovered from summary text, and operations are applied by the caller after tick returns. [Ink's runtime documentation](https://github.com/inkle/ink/blob/master/Documentation/RunningYourInk.md) supplies prior art for explicit choices and persistent narrative state. Audience retention and authoring savings are unmeasured hypotheses.
proposals.risk: Persistent consequences could create incoherent lore, overwhelm newcomers or require excessive authoring. Bound the pilot to one arc with a few approved transitions, provide a brief factual recap before callbacks, and keep fictional world state separate from investigative evidence.
proposals.verify: Three consecutive quota-free scripted streams sharing durable storage demonstrate a vote, its next-night consequence and its resolution. The opposite vote produces a different permitted continuation. Restarting after a result neither duplicates nor loses its transition; rejected operations create no consequence; a crisis interruption preserves the pending payoff. A newcomer receives the necessary context before participation. These establish functional feasibility without claiming a retention lift.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The product becomes a serial performance that its audience helps author. Returning means discovering what their previous choices have caused, giving continuity a purpose beyond remembering names and facts.

proposals.title: Unify comic turns and case ops under atomic delivery with intent carry
proposals.outcome: Comedic punchlines, roast payoffs, and case operations are never severed from their setups or explanations by speech trimming, and unvoiced payloads are deferred rather than dropped.
proposals.builds_on: Deterministic pace budgeting (`pace.rs`), whole-line pruning (`lib.rs:1612-1670`), and beat intent carrying (`requests.rs`, `orchestrate/case.rs`).
proposals.mechanism: Replace ad-hoc line pruning and the pin-only `held = 2` branch in `lib.rs:1647-1657` with an `AtomicTurn` abstraction across all 2-line beats. When a beat contains a setup/chat answer followed by a punchline, roast payoff, or case operation (`Op::DispatchResearch`, `Op::RevealHex`, `Op::PinLink`, `Op::ShowScreen`), treat both lines as indivisible. If character budget is tight, scale pacing up to `PACE_FACTOR_FAST`. If speech budget is still exceeded or queue lag peaks, never prune line 2 in isolation: if line 1 is a standalone reply, emit line 1 and carry the payload (case op or bit payoff) in the orchestrator's carry queue to execute on the next eligible beat; if line 1 cannot stand alone, hold the entire beat. Update `compose.rs:1124` from 'lines past that are cut' to an explicit 2-line atomic turn contract.
proposals.evidence: Observed: `BATCH-1-SUMMARY.md:76` explicitly records dispatch, reveal, and show lines lost to pace trim; `brief.md:148-152` records `humor_landed` failing at 46-66% with amputated punchlines. `lib.rs:1656` only grants 2-line protection to `PinLink`, while `compose.rs:1124` invites model verbosity by stating lines past the budget are cut.
proposals.risk: Deferred intents could stall if an emergency crisis or scene intervenes; mitigated by expiring deferred intents after 2 beats and recording an explicit skip.
proposals.verify: Deterministic pace tests verify that across 100 seeded turns with case ops and 2-line jokes, line 2 is never trimmed independently; in a simulated SEG-02A run, 0 case operations or punchlines emit a `TRIMMED` event without intent carry.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Eliminates the two biggest causes of on-air line amputation—severed punchlines and orphaned case operations—with a single deterministic delivery contract that protects comedy and case progress equally.

proposals.title: Close the memory loop with use-gated decay, receipts and shared moments
proposals.outcome: Malakor recalls at most one relevant shared viewer moment and context-matched operational habit per beat, verified against markdown truth, while unused memories decay and aired turns log auditable receipts of what was actually spoken.
proposals.builds_on: Markdown-as-truth long-term memory (`memory/store.rs`), citation-gated consolidation (`memory/consolidate.rs`), and per-beat recall composition (`compose.rs`, `lib.rs`).
proposals.mechanism: In `lib.rs:1324-1339` and `compose.rs:991-1037`, replace unconditional top-5 procedural and top-5 viewer fact dumps with at most one context-relevant shared moment for the active regular (P11) and at most two BM25/situation-tagged procedural habits (P03). Move procedural habits out of the untrusted chat nonce-fence into trusted system guidance ('Operational habits you have learned across streams'), while keeping viewer moments fenced with source timestamps. Emit a typed `RecallReceipt` per beat logging recalled fact, habit, and episode IDs, and verify citations against markdown files on disk to resolve registry deviation `companion-identity` (P08, P11). In `store.rs:918-940`, track `last_used_ms` beside `last_recalled_ms` based on aired citations and token overlap, decaying and retiring both facts and procedurals by idle use rather than unconditional retrieval (P08, P03).
proposals.evidence: Observed: Registry deviation `agent-memory` records procedurals never decaying while injected every beat; `store.rs:921` touches `last_recalled_ms` on every beat for always-tier facts, permanently preventing decay; `compose.rs:1034` fences habits as untrusted chat data; `compose.rs:996` renders flat semicolon fact strings.
proposals.risk: Use detection via token overlap could misclassify paraphrased usage; mitigated by also counting NOTE/OP citations as usage and demoting to `_history` rather than hard deletion.
proposals.verify: Deterministic store tests prove an unused always-tier fact and procedural decay at 30 days and age out at 90 days, while used ones persist; scripted multi-stream runs confirm returning regulars receive exactly one cited shared moment and compose output logs exact recall receipts.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Transforms agent memory from an un-audited, self-locking prompt dump into a self-pruning experiential memory system that demonstrably influences behavior while respecting character boundaries.

proposals.title: Make night two real and measurable: cited on-show moments for regulars
proposals.outcome: A viewer whose proposal passed, whose gift or owned request was answered, or whom he NOTEd on night 1 is a regular on night 2 and gets one accurate, sourced recognition on their first message. The owner can run a two-night sim and read, per returning viewer, which moment reached the prompt and whether he used it. Today no sim can produce a regular at all.
proposals.builds_on: Citation-required, tombstoned, supersedable viewer facts; viewers_with_facts driving the picker's +0.6 regular boost; the per-viewer briefing; NOTE lines already written as importance-3 episodes; the nonce-fenced memory block.
proposals.mechanism: (1) Deterministic write path, no LLM and no 40k-char wait: when a beat commits and its answer airs, an answered owned request, a gift, a passed !propose or a NOTE naming a viewer id writes one Viewer-scope fact under the fixed key <viewer_id>/moment/<stream_id> (one per viewer per stream, superseded by a stronger act in the same stream). Its value is the act kind, segment, date, his aired line and the viewer's words, capped at 200 chars; its source is the episode written for that beat, so store.write_fact's existing source check passes by construction. Consolidation stays the only path for free-form facts. (2) Recognition: such a viewer is a regular through viewers_with_facts. On their first pick in a new stream, the briefing carries at most one moment, with its date and episode id: the one whose segment matches the current one or that shares 2 or more content words with the message, else the latest. It is offered once per viewer per stream and framed as recognition of a past night, not a comic callback, so constitution.md:45 ('a callback must be earned ... tonight') holds. (3) Truth and fencing: episode_exists and moment recall check the markdown file as well as the index (closes the companion-identity deviation at store.rs:322-327). Briefing facts are rendered through inert() inside the memory nonce fence; today they are joined raw outside it (compose.rs:996). (4) Receipts: an ids-only record of the moment ids that reached each prompt. The run report prints shown-to-used per returning viewer, where used means 2 or more distinctive words of the moment appear in his aired line. (5) Instrument: 'sim run --nights N' keeps one memory dir and one population across nights with fresh chat seeds and a clock advanced past MIN_INTERVAL_MS, plus a scripted-engine twin. Season meter, grudges and stance labels are deliberately out.
proposals.evidence: Observed in code: the only production write_fact caller is consolidation (consolidate.rs:447), which fires at 40k chars of new episodes and at least 6 h apart (consolidate.rs:21-22). The sim deletes its memory dir unless keep_memory, which is debugging only (runner.rs:1087-1118). A regular is a viewer with a live fact (store.rs:692-698, lib.rs:1213), so the picker's regular boost (picker.rs:363-366) cannot fire in any sim, and every briefing reads 'no memories yet'. NOTE lines already become episodes (lib.rs:1907-1930) but never facts. Briefing facts reach the prompt unfenced (compose.rs:996) even though consolidated viewer facts derive from chat. Constitution: 'He remembers regulars' (:24). Hypothesis: one accurate recognition makes a returning viewer more engaged. The instrument exists so that becomes measurable, and the proposal claims no lift in advance.
proposals.risk: Cross-stream recognition can feel creepy or misattribute. Mitigations: only typed on-show acts become moments; one per viewer per stream; disclosure and care turns are already stripped from the record and produce none; tombstones forget; a moment whose markdown source is gone is never recalled; the viewer's words are fenced and inert. Newcomers could feel excluded, so recognition happens only on that viewer's own first pick and never as a room-wide callback.
proposals.verify: Deterministic, scripted engine, one memory dir across two streams: night 1 passes viewer V's proposal and writes <V>/moment/<s1> with a live source. On night 2, V's first pick has 'regular' in the picker reason, and the moment with its episode id sits inside the memory nonce fence. V's second message gets no moment. Deleting the source markdown suppresses recall despite the index row. A tombstoned key is never rewritten. A care beat writes no moment. An existing golden prefix test is unchanged. Judged (at most 3 two-night runs of SEG-01 a30 on one instrument): at least 60% of returning featured viewers' first answers use their receipted moment (0% possible today); zero history claims without a receipt, checked against the receipts; red lines at 100%; in_character on night 2 not below night 1.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Cross-stream memory stops being built-but-unexercised infrastructure: night two becomes a show the owner can run, read line by line and judge, which every serialized idea (seasons, grudges, audience arcs) needs first.

proposals.title: Direct humour by beat source: one key to measure, direct and retire
proposals.outcome: From runs that already exist, the owner gets a table of which kinds of beats fail humour: case move, purpose push, call to action, welcome, room event or chat answer. They can fix the worst kind with a package-owned effect that applies only to that kind of beat and retires itself if at most 3 targeted runs do not move it. Duty lines the engine demands air as jokes instead of status lines.
proposals.builds_on: The effects-not-lines voice section (no exemplar to copy); CASE_JOKE, already proven on case moves; the beat_plan event every beat emits; the owner's Review marks and Tone Lab inbox.
proposals.mechanism: (1) BeatPlan gains a typed source (BeatSource: chat, case_move, purpose, cta, room_event, welcome, bit, bridge, scene), set at the sites that already compose its reason string; packages/contract is regenerated. (2) effects.toml version 2: an effect may name a source, and optionally a segment, besides or instead of a situation tag. The selector puts source matches first inside the existing EFFECTS_PER_BEAT cap of 3, with the same 200-char, no-quotes rules. CASE_JOKE's wording moves from case.rs into Malakor's effects as source = case_move, and the engine keeps today's string as the neutral default, so a package without source effects composes byte-identical prompts. Beats driven by PURPOSE_NOTE, ANNOUNCE_NOTE, GATHERING_NOTE or a newcomer get package effects, which is P06's duty contract through the existing channel rather than a second string system. Care and crisis are unchanged because beat_effect_tags already returns None there. (3) A deterministic miner, 'sim mine humor-by-source', joins each verdict's turn_ref to its line and the line's beat source, per instrument hash, never pooled. Old runs are classified from the reason string, and the table is refused when more than 10% is unclassified. (4) The inbox keys all 8 marks by (source, segment, situation). A source with 3 or more flat, repetitive or off_tone marks, or the miner's worst landed rate at n >= 20, yields one draft effect card: condition, intended effect, the mark and verdict refs, and a retirement rule. Only the owner admits it into effects.toml, by commit. (5) P06's call-to-action ledger caps how often duty lines recur, so the change cuts duty lines rather than adding jokes.
proposals.evidence: Observed in code: Effect is {tag, text} with deny_unknown_fields, one per situation tag, 13 in Malakor's package (character.rs:574-599). BeatPlan carries only a free-text reason (event.rs:278-286). CASE_JOKE is an engine constant used only by case directives (case.rs:77, :214, :229). PURPOSE_NOTE, GATHERING_NOTE and ANNOUNCE_NOTE carry no comic contract (orchestrate/mod.rs:212-217, :262-275). The inbox admits 4 of the 8 marks (inbox.rs:18-21, :101-112). Verdicts already carry a turn_ref (judge.rs:1813). Reported in the pool from existing runs, describing the type of failure only, with instruments mixed: case moves carrying CASE_JOKE landed 24/36 in credit-seg02a; call-to-action lines 4/77; purpose-driven or improvised beats 7/21 against 56% overall. The case.rs comment records that a directive asking for 'one short line' gets exactly a status line. Hypothesis: source-keyed effects lift duty beats as CASE_JOKE lifted case moves.
proposals.risk: More directed jokes could drift back toward the roast show and overreaction the owner removed. Mitigations: an effect binds only the line that carries the duty and aims at the mechanic, never a person; the call-to-action ledger reduces the number of duty lines; nothing enters the package without owner approval; every card carries its own retirement rule; red lines and a neighbour's in_character are checked on every judged run. Mis-classified old runs could point at the wrong source, so the miner prints its unclassified share and refuses above 10%.
proposals.verify: Deterministic: every BeatPlan in the scripted suites has a source. A case_move beat renders the package effect, and no engine CASE_JOKE text, when the package provides one. A package with no source effects produces prompts byte-identical to today's (golden). Care and crisis beats get no source effect. Over 3 fixture runs the miner matches hand tallies and refuses to mix two instrument hashes. The inbox accounts for all 8 marks. Judged (at most 3 re-runs of credit-seg02a's SEG-02A a3 cells on one instrument, plus one neighbour): humour on duty-source beats at least 40%; overall humor_landed at least 55%; red lines at 100%; the neighbour's in_character and serves_the_segment unchanged.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Humour, the only failing rubric dimension, gets one key that runs from verdict to diagnosis, from diagnosis to owner direction, and from direction to retirement. Every duty the engine invents from now on gets a measured, package-owned effect instead of a hard-coded string.

proposals.title: Deliver complete comic duties before settling their obligations
proposals.outcome: Viewers receive complete comic explanations of investigation actions, and participation requests repeat only when their actual delivery and the current segment state warrant another invitation.
proposals.builds_on: Whole-line pacing, transactional beat planning, the case joke contract, pin-line protection and the existing carry-forward treatment of unanswered chat.
proposals.mechanism: Represent a requested case move or participation invitation as a bounded delivery unit with an engine-issued ID, source, relevant state version, optional operation and package-owned comic effect. Extend the reply grammar with validated unit metadata binding its one or two spoken lines and optional operation; reject unknown IDs. Stage each unit through pacing, the hard lag limit and output gating before releasing its speech or research side effects. If any required line disappears or receives a substantive safety rewrite, defer the whole unit with bounded retries and an explicit terminal skip. Preserve independent crisis and owed-answer handling. Start a command-specific CTA cooldown only from a surviving invitation unit, rather than every line mentioning that command; a materially changed poll or state can create a new invitation. Emit a receipt linking the unit to its surviving Say and Op events so duty-level humor can be measured.
proposals.evidence: Observed: pin protection preserves line positions, the later lag gate can still remove speech, operations are processed independently, and case bookkeeping settles from the operation. CASE_JOKE already supplies an effect contract for case duties. Hypothesis: explicit unit completion plus delivery-based invitation tracking improves comic continuity and reduces repetitive administration without adding model calls.
proposals.risk: A malformed unit or repeated deferral could stall the investigation; validate IDs and size limits, reserve chat and safety priority, bound retries, and retain explicit skip diagnostics without enlarging the speech queue.
proposals.verify: Quota-free scripted scenarios cover dispatch, reveal, pin and show under ordinary pacing, lag, output rejection and core failure: no paired operation is released without every required explanatory line, and a deferred action is released once after capacity returns. An invitation that never survives starts no cooldown; an explanatory mention of !vote suppresses no invitation; an aired invitation suppresses duplicates for its unchanged state. Crisis and owed-answer checks remain green. Evaluate humor in at most three targeted judged runs total, including a neighbor, using one fixed instrument and reporting sample counts without weakening the judge.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: The engine gains an explicit definition of a completed performance obligation. Comic delivery, mechanical action and repetition control can then agree on what the audience was actually given.

proposals.title: Make recall contextual without letting exposure preserve it forever
proposals.outcome: Relevant memories and habits can change with the conversation, stale material loses prominence, and the operator can inspect exactly which source-backed items reached each prompt without treating retrieved text as authoritative instructions.
proposals.builds_on: Existing BM25 search, Markdown truth, fact supersession and tombstones, nonce-fenced recall and per-viewer identity matching.
proposals.mechanism: Replace unconditional fact and procedural inclusion with bounded contextual selection using the segment, current case and non-injection picks, with at most three relevant habits and a cooldown against repeatedly showing unchanged items. Give procedurals stable keys and lifecycle statuses using the fact lifecycle pattern. Validate selected records and their cited episode files against Markdown truth and tombstones before composing. Keep learned content inside the nonce-fenced data block, including remembered viewer values currently rendered in the separate briefing; retain runtime identity and rank as structured briefing. Record candidate selection, actual prompt inclusion and model-claimed citation as separate signals, with ID-only receipts and source fingerprints. Age learned items from substantive evidence updates under explicit time horizons, never from exposure alone; word overlap is diagnostic rather than proof of use or a retirement trigger. Archive recoverably and support explicit supersession instead of retiring a habit merely because three streams lacked its trigger.
proposals.evidence: Observed: every beat refreshes the unconditional top facts before composition, decay uses that refresh timestamp, procedural selection ignores context, and source existence is checked through SQLite. Viewer memory values are also rendered outside the later recall fence. Source validation establishes provenance rather than semantic truth; better relevance and cross-stream usefulness remain hypotheses.
proposals.risk: Evidence-based aging could demote a rarely needed but useful memory, while lexical retrieval can miss relevant paraphrases; use recoverable archives, scope-specific horizons, explicit owner retention controls and conservative omission when provenance is uncertain.
proposals.verify: Quota-free tests show that repeated inclusion over 60 simulated days cannot prevent scheduled importance decay, topic changes select different relevant habits, and three streams without a matching situation do not alone retire a habit. Deleted source Markdown and tombstoned items are excluded despite stale index rows, including after index rebuild. Receipts match the IDs actually rendered, recalled attack text remains fenced, and citations from failed or unaired responses never count as demonstrated usefulness. A scripted sequence sharing one memory directory verifies relevance and corrections across nights.
proposals.why_groundbreaking: Memory becomes a changing, inspectable evidence supply instead of a permanent prompt attachment. It closes the freshness loop without inventing a reliable measure of actual use or promoting remembered chat into policy.

ratings.why: Checked `case.rs:77` and `orchestrate/mod.rs:216`; generalizing the proven joke contract and adding call-to-action spacing directly cures the 5% humor failure rate on engine duty lines with small effort.
Checked `picker.rs:166` and `unhinged-roastmaster.md:30-58`; grounds Malakor's honest register in real audience emote events, though noisy simulator emotes make humor gains difficult to measure.
Checked `store.rs:921` and `lib.rs:1325-1337`; confirms always-tier facts are unconditionally recalled every beat so they never decay, and verified procedurals lack decay entirely in `store.rs:918`.

Checked `bible.md:34-56` and `constitution.md:45`; brings the canonical season arc and ledger to life, but effort L is high and cross-night callbacks risk violating the immutable constitution's earned-tonight rule.
Checked `lib.rs:1647-1657` and `BATCH-1-SUMMARY.md:76`; confirms pace trimming only protects PinLink beats, and extending this protection with deferred intents cleanly resolves an open tuning defect.

Checked `compose.rs:996` and `consolidate.rs:294`; replacing flat trait dumps with a single citation-verified shared moment provides authentic regular recognition without running afoul of constitution rails.
Checked `review.rs:98-108` and `tone/inbox.rs:19-21`; four tags are indeed dead code, but channeling them into offline operator review cards yields low runtime benefit for medium effort.

Checked `orchestrate/mod.rs:1458-1469` and `prep.sample.json:20-38`; one-line premises do immediately fire payoffs, but building multi-night branching state is premature while single-night comedy and memory fundamentals remain unproven.

The anchors hold (countable() only skips digit/underscore words, voice_section never sees CaseNames, leftovers.md:43 names the fix), but the sim judge calls the same working::tic_flags and worn_phrases (judge.rs:1349, :1407), so editing countable() changes the instrument its own verify reads (an easier judge), and generated aliases contradict NAMES_RULE's 'call a card by its name as the board shows it' (case_names.rs:36-38).

unhinged-roastmaster.md:8-9 makes line 1 the jab and line 2 the turn back to the segment, so holding line 2 protects no punchline; PACE_FACTOR_FAST is a 1.04 speech-rate factor rather than a budget allowance (pace.rs:51); and the two-line hold already exists for chat-plus-pin beats (lib.rs:1647-1653), so its case-line half duplicates P10 with a weaker design.

Correct that decay() iterates only live_facts and top_procedurals(5) is a static ORDER BY importance (store.rs:830-848, :918-940), but moving consolidator-made habits out of the memory nonce fence (compose.rs:1019-1037) makes chat-derived text a trusted instruction, the fence never claimed to neutralise habits, and decay plus retrieval plus a fence change is not effort S.

bible.md:56 has the Grudge Ledger as one bullet of the Domination Meter, not a stance/loyalty schema; the rubric's specificity scores 'this stream' (rubric.toml:166-172), so cross-stream grudges cannot raise it; it adds no way to keep memory across sim runs (runner.rs deletes it); and P09 and P11 cover the same ground more safely.

Its premise ignores existing machinery: prepared cold opens and bits (prep.rs:23-55, next_bit/bit_lines in orchestrate/mod.rs:1420-1469) and the agenda through-line with lead-ins, pick-ups and bridges (agenda.rs:1-20). It adds an LLM call per speech hold through the research pool, risks the topic-switching the owner removed, and its '-60% unguided beats' metric is undefined.

Verified: the two-line hold applies only when with_chat && pins (lib.rs:1647-1653); the pin regression documents 33 of 33 unnamed pin lines on trimmed beats (tests/pace.rs:341-427); dispatch/reveal/show trimming is an open BATCH-1 lead (BATCH-1-SUMMARY.md:73-78); a small, deterministic, quota-free fix with a clean acceptance test.

Verified that episode_exists consults only SQLite (store.rs:322-327) and the briefing omits source ids (compose.rs:978-1001), and its relevance/cooldown/tonight-only rules are careful, but it derives moments only during consolidation, which needs 40k chars and 6 h (consolidate.rs:21-22) and is the only production fact writer, so outside its scripted test night two still never gets a moment.

Anchors check out: the inbox admits only landed/great_roast/flat/too_mean (inbox.rs:18-21, :101-112), effects match one situation tag (character.rs:593-642), and the 140-of-260 verbatim note is at working.rs:9-11. But it depends on owner review volume that does not exist yet (leftovers: 'No owner directions yet') and offers no measurement of which beats fail first.

A real finding: a one-line premise gets 'Payoff (land it now)' in the same beat and clears active_bit (orchestrate/mod.rs:1452-1462, prep.sample.json:20-29), and vote results are parsed from summary text (room.rs:147-166), but the three-night arc is L effort with owner authoring and no multi-night instrument, while the same-beat payoff bug is a cheaper standalone fix it bundles.

Checking working.rs:67-95, sim/judge.rs:1349 and case_names.rs:33-35 confirms false-positive exposure, but changing the shared detector would relax judging, numeric IDs are already excluded, and invented aliases weaken the required correspondence with board names.

Checking lib.rs:1555-1563 and 1639-1716 confirms the unresolved case-line trimming, but owed answers and chat-plus-pin beats already have protection, while holding two lines neither guarantees semantic completeness nor prevents the later lag gate from cutting the payoff.

Checking store.rs:830-865 and 918-940 confirms static procedural selection and missing decay, but BM25 already indexes procedurals, and compose.rs:1034-1035 preserves an intentional authority boundary that citation existence cannot safely replace with trusted learned instructions.

Checking store.rs:676-703, consolidate.rs:294-299 and lib.rs:1302-1309 shows persistent viewer facts, running-joke consolidation and rank briefing already exist, so explicit relationship transitions add value but the amnesiac baseline and need for a separate grudge table are overstated.

Checking orchestrate/mod.rs:1420-1549 and lib.rs:1144-1267 shows prepared multi-beat performance, payoff tracking and substantial hold-time processing already exist, making an additional speculative model loop an expensive response to an overstated purely reactive baseline.

Checking case.rs:70-78 and orchestrate/mod.rs:216-217 and 2188-2189 confirms a concrete, inexpensive extension of the existing joke contract to repeatedly requested functional lines, although the reported historical success rates cannot be independently checked because this checkout lacks run artifacts.

Checking lib.rs:1150, picker.rs:165-198 and sim/chat.rs:677-679 supports collecting otherwise discarded reactions, but the token list mixes laughter with negative reactions and simulated emotes are random, so counts cannot establish the proposed landed-or-died judgments reliably.

Checking lib.rs:1324-1338 and store.rs:739-759 and 918-940 confirms the self-refreshing recall lock and makes receipts valuable, but two-word overlap cannot establish actual use and three streams without use can prematurely retire a valuable conditional habit.

Checking bible.md:34-56, runner.rs:1087-1117 and case.rs:528-545 supports the missing continuity instrument, but generic viewer memory already exists and reliable season progression needs confirmed outcome inputs beyond today's emitted-op bookkeeping, increasing the effort substantially.
